sources.locator: "Siege of Crema (1514)", revision 1370740461, § Background, 1512–1514: Shifting alliances
the work the article cites for that sentence

explanation: The Crema article says why the town was worth a siege: "Crema remained heavily militarized, serving as a Venetian bridgehead to reclaim territories lost after Agnadello", and again, of the Senate, "determined to recover all territories lost post-Agnadello". The loss at Agnadello is the condition that made Crema a Venetian bridgehead and therefore a target. `precondition-of` and not `caused`: the article makes Agnadello the state of affairs the siege happened inside, not its trigger. Probable: Wikipedia, with the work Wikipedia itself cites for the sentence beside it — which is a second author and not a second reading, so the confidence does not rise.
